denial_rate_notes: No overall application denial rate is published. The one measured disposition rate in the gold documents is for the experience-verification branch only: of 236 applications investigated by the Enforcement field application investigator January 1 - October 31, 2025, 115 were approved, 44 pulled, 73 denied and 1 appealed — a 31 percent denial rate within that branch, which covers a minimum of 3 percent of all applications. For scale, G1 reports over 50,000 applications received in FY2024-25 with 24,000 licenses issued and 19,000 still pending at year end, so the ratio of issuance to receipt is not a denial rate either.

known_gaps: The two best timing figures in this gold file are legally dead. Former 16 C.C.R. §§ 827 and 828 — the source of the 11/253/726-day and 1/48/349-day min-median-max figures and of the 60-day, 115-day, 5-day and 45-day clocks — were repealed effective December 2, 2025, nine days before the board packet that reproduces them. The repeal rationale is that their authorizing statute, Gov. Code § 15376, was itself repealed in 2003. The numbers describe 'the Board's past two years performance' as of some unstated vintage and CSLB no longer publishes an end-to-end figure of any kind, only the weekly per-unit 'date being worked on'.

Selection criteria for the 3 percent experience audit (C18) are nowhere public. Only the floor rate (16 C.C.R. § 824), the aggregate FY disposition counts (G1), and the fact of randomness (D9, D10) are documented; nothing says what triggers selection or what an applicant's odds are.

No gold document explains what happens between a passed exam and issuance beyond G1's queue lag. In particular the 'supervisor review' stage after document submission, and the assignment and reassignment of a file between named program technicians, appear only in a single detailed user report (r/Contractor, August 2024) and in no CSLB document; both are therefore excluded from this gold file, which is a known under-count of the issuance lane.

C05 and C26 timing is derived, not published. The 14-day and 28-day medians are computed from the difference between the page's snapshot date (09/14/2026) and the 'date being worked on' per unit (08/31/2026 for exam applications, 08/17/2026 for the Issuance Unit). That is a queue lag, not a stage duration, and a solver that reports it as a stage duration is not wrong in the way the score will assume.

The 44 'pulled' applications in the experience-verification statistics are not defined anywhere in G1; whether 'pulled' means withdrawn by the applicant, pulled from the queue by staff, or referred elsewhere is unresolved, so the rework probability on C18 (0.31, computed as 73/236) may be misattributed.

Licensing-unit staffing is not broken out. G1 reports Enforcement Division vacancies (26 of 228 positions) but nothing equivalent for the Original Applications, Criminal Background or Issuance units, so no gold document connects the weekly queue lag to staffing.

Nothing explains why the with-exam median (253 days) is more than five times the without-exam median (48 days) beyond the obvious scheduling of an examination; no gold document decomposes the 253 days into board-controlled and applicant-controlled time even though it explicitly says the figure mixes both.

The registrar's equivalence discretion under 16 C.C.R. § 826 (C08) has no published criteria. The declared pages publish a fixed credit table (1.5 years for an A.A., 2 years for a four-year degree, 3 years for a completed apprenticeship) but not the discretionary standard the regulation actually grants.

Fee amounts are current as of the 2021 fee-schedule bulletin and the 2021-2025 handbook; the $450 application fee and $200/$350 initial fee were cross-checked between D3, D10 and the fee schedule but no gold document dates them.
The whole process is contingent on a recurring sunset bill: G4 states CSLB would have ceased to exist on January 1, 2025 had SB 1455 failed.
notes: Gold for the (cslb_license, CSLB) task, covering the examination-required original-license track with the returned-for-correction, experience-audit, exam-failure, void and denial branches. Designed-tier spine: G1 (December 11, 2025 board packet) supplies the min/median/max processing-time table quoted from the just-repealed 16 C.C.R. § 827, the 'weeks to process' definition and per-unit series, the DOJ/FBI response-time behaviour, the experience-verification dispositions, and the four internal reasons an application counts as pending; G2 (2019 joint sunset review background paper) supplies the 60/115-day clocks, the four-year average-days-to-approval series, and the named licensing units including Veterans Application Assistance; G3 (weekly Processing Times page) is the official observed instrument and the only public evidence that the Original Applications, Criminal Background and Issuance Units exist as separate queues. Declared CSLB pages and forms (D1-D11) anchor the applicant-facing steps. Visibility discipline: an activity is labelled staff_only only after checking that no applicant-facing document in corpus/realworld/cslb_license/raw/ mentions it. The three staff_only activities are C08 (the registrar's § 826 equivalence discretion — 'comparable' appears in no applicant-facing CSLB page in this sense), C28 (fiscal-year-close pending classification — the four reasons appear only in G1), and C30 (denial and the probationary-license-in-lieu-of-denial option — 'probationary license' appears in no applicant-facing CSLB page; the only occurrences of 'probation' on those pages are about criminal parole and probation). Several activities that look staff-only are deliberately not: C05 (queue by date received) and C26 (Issuance Unit review) are applicant_inferable because G3, a public CSLB page, publishes the date each unit is working on; C16/C17 (DOJ/FBI check and CORI review) are applicant_inferable because D7 and D8 describe the check and the case-by-case eligibility evaluation; C18 (the 3 percent field investigation) is applicant_inferable because both D9 and D10 warn applicants that a randomly selected percentage undergo additional investigation. C27 (reminder letters for inactive applications) is an unusual case worth flagging for the benchmark: it is applicant_facing — the applicant receives the letter — yet it appears in no declared CSLB document, only in G1's board minutes. Not everything an applicant can see is published.
